category_title: Average-level readers engaging in balanced discourse
student_description: This is an average-level reader who tends to provide literal, physical descriptions or unelaborated claims during reading conferences. They struggle to spontaneously generate higher-level inferences or justifications when given generic prompts, but they respond highly effectively to specific, targeted follow-up questions that scaffold their thinking.

criteria.rationale: To build the student's inferential capacity without causing frustration, the tutor must balance literal support with increasing cognitive challenge over time.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include a strategy for deliberately adjusting the ratio of lower-level (literal) to higher-level (inferential) questions based on the student's ongoing reading level and readiness.

criteria.rationale: The student needs sustained practice and explicit modeling to learn how to elaborate and engage in deeper literary discourse independently.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate structured tools or frameworks (such as SEM-R bookmarks or specific question sets) to model follow-up questions and systematically increase the student's opportunities for elaborated talk.
